Chapter 10: A New Identity—Living as One Who Has Been Changed
After a crisis, or a big transformation, there's this huge question that hangs in the air—who am I now? When the old roles, the familiar titles, even the stories you've told yourself for years start to fade away, it can feel like standing at the edge of something completely new and a little bit uncertain. Maybe you've been forgiven, started over, or finally let go of a past mistake. So, what does it really mean to live as someone who's been changed?
Well, there's no magic switch. It's not about a single moment, but about the choices you make, day in and day out. Every morning, you get another chance to live out the values that matter most—like honesty, humility, service, and grace. Sure, that old need for approval or recognition might still pop up. But now, it doesn't control everything you do.
Picture this: you're sitting with a young person who's facing their own hard times. Maybe you're mentoring them, just sharing your story. And suddenly, it hits you—the things that really matter aren't found in all your successes, but in your failures. Being willing to talk about your mistakes, to be open about the rocky parts of your journey, that’s where the real strength is. Sometimes, the greatest thing you can offer isn’t advice or a quick fix. It’s just being there—truly present—walking alongside someone as they find their way.
Out in the community, this new sense of identity gets tested again and again. There’ll be moments of doubt, times when you feel insecure, or even times when you miss the comfort of your old life. But every time you choose to act with integrity, to serve, to show a little bit of grace, that new identity grows stronger.
Most folks think identity is set in stone—shaped by your past or your current situation. But in reality, it’s much more flexible than that. Who you are is shaped by the stories you tell yourself, the values you decide to stand by, and the relationships you build. Transformation isn’t something you check off a list—it’s a journey. And every single day, you get the chance to step a little closer to the person you want to become.
Of course, the past is still there. It reminds you of what you’ve lost, and maybe even what you’ve learned. But it doesn’t get to define who you are now. When your new identity is rooted in things like faith, humility, and service, it becomes a real source of hope—not just for you, but for anyone else searching for a way forward.
